findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and uses wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The grant shortcut in an encoded id like 'onrtac:<uuid>' occupies characters 4-5 (0-based substring(4,6)), but the matcher checks substring(3,5), i.e. 'ta' for authorization_code. It also returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut and only proceeds when it differs. Consequently expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken will fail for correctly encoded tokens and can pass for tokens from the wrong grant, so the new encoding is not actually verified by these tests.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI implemented by extensions outside this repository. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method makes every existing custom factory fail to compile and, if deployed as an old binary, throw AbstractMethodError when Keycloak enumerates grant factories in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit/getShortcutByGrantType. It should be a default method (e.g. returning a fallback/'na' or a derived 2-char value) so existing grants keep issuing tokens.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
findings.body: The PR deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor while adding grantType extraction to the main constructor. Any grant/token-exchange code or custom extension that wrapped an existing Context via the copy constructor will no longer compile and old binaries will throw NoSuchMethodError. The copy constructor should be retained (and updated to copy grantType) or explicitly deprecated rather than removed.

findings.title: Token issuance now hard-fails for unknown or custom grant types
findings.body: TokenManager.initToken unconditionally calls encodeTokenId for every access token. getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext only falls back to 'na' when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is null; if the attribute holds any value not registered as an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (custom grants, internal/direct token creation paths that set a grant string, or grants whose factory returns no shortcut) getShortcutByGrantType returns null and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException, aborting token issuance entirely instead of encoding the token with the 'na' unknown marker.

findings.title: Documented 3-letter shortcuts are incompatible with the fixed 6-character decoder
findings.body: The getShortcut() Javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes session(2)+token(2)+grant(shortcut) and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6. A factory following the documented contract and returning a 3-letter (or 1-letter) shortcut produces ids that can be issued but never decoded, throwing IllegalArgumentException on parsing. Either validate at postInit that every shortcut is exactly 2 characters and fail fast, or fix the Javadoc/format to state and enforce that requirement.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' instead of checking the rawTokenId parameter. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, later producing an encoded id ending in ':null' or an NPE downstream, and decoding such an id yields a context whose raw id is the literal string 'null'. The second check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: Null or duplicate shortcuts put into ConcurrentHashMap cause NPE or misleading startup failure
findings.body: postInit unconditionally does grantsByShortcuts.put(gtf.getShortcut(), grantName) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut) on ConcurrentHashMaps. If any grant factory (in particular a legacy/custom one given a default getShortcut, or one returning null) returns null, ConcurrentHashMap throws NullPointerException during startup with no indication of which grant caused it. Shortcut nullness/length/uniqueness should be validated explicitly with the grant id in the error message before inserting.
